note: The scorer's own output for the MIND NRMS submission (mind_nrms_submission.zip) on Codabench competition 13967, transcribed verbatim from predictions/Codabench_results/MIND/scoring_result/{metadata,scores.json}. MIND's scorer returns only the four headline ranking metrics plus a metadata block -- no per-day, sentiment or coverage breakdown exists here the way it does for EB-NeRD's scorer, so this file is shorter than leaderboard_ebnerd_2469.json by construction, not by omission.

scorer_metadata.note: elapsedTime is the scoring program's run time (about 11.2 minutes). exitCode 0 is the scorer completing successfully. ingestionElapsedTime and ingestionExitCode are null in the returned file; MIND's scorer reports no ingestion step for this submission.

offline_comparison.note: The offline harness predicted this submission's four ranking metrics on mind_small's test split (n=2,000, reports/metrics/rerank_eval.json, nrms_category_aware) before it was scored. TWO of four land inside the offline 95% bootstrap interval, two do not -- unlike A1's EB-NeRD semantic submission, where all four landed inside. Reported honestly rather than only citing the two that agree: nDCG@5 and nDCG@10 (which score only the top of the ranking) fall inside their intervals; AUC and MRR (which are sensitive to where the clicked article sits among ALL candidates, not just the top few) fall outside -- AUC above the upper bound, MRR below the lower bound. A plausible reason, not verified: MINDlarge_test's candidate-list-length distribution may differ from mind_small's, which would move AUC/MRR (rank-sensitive across the whole list) more than nDCG@5/@10 (which only look at the top of it). A 2,000-impression sample of a 73,152-impression corpus predicting a 2,370,727-impression, differently-sized corpus disagreeing on two of four metrics is not a surprising outcome to extrapolate across that gap -- it is the kind of disagreement the offline interval exists to make visible rather than to rule out.

comparison_to_a1_submissions.note: NRMS minus each earlier MIND submission, per metric. NRMS is ahead of the A1 hybrid on AUC ONLY; the hybrid is slightly ahead on MRR, nDCG@5 and nDCG@10. Reported per metric so the AUC gain is not read as a uniform improvement.
